q: A diesel shop apprentice explains to a fleet driver, in plain words and without jargon, why the truck needs a fuel filter change. This shows:
o: effective oral communication with people from varied cultures and backgrounds

q: Which oral communication habit works best when a customer describes a symptom?
o: Listening, then repeating the symptom back to confirm it

q: Marisol writes a repair order that lists the complaint, the cause found and the fix, in clear sentences. This shows:
o: effective written communication in the diesel shop

q: A written repair order should include the complaint, the cause and the correction so that:
o: the next technician can follow the work

q: A student measures a bolt in millimeters and a shaft in inches and converts between them with a chart. She is showing:
o: math skills and precision measurement with metric and customary units

o: describing the function of major components of diesel powered vehicles

o: heat created by compressing the air in the cylinder

q: A technician explains that the air brake system, the steering gear and the transmission make up parts of a heavy truck's chassis. She is:
o: describing the function of chassis components

q: On a heavy truck, air brakes are commonly used because they:
o: can be applied reliably over long trailers and heavy loads

o: precision measurement procedures to diagnose component wear

o: replace or machine the part as directed

q: Before using a floor jack under a truck frame, a technician sets jack stands and checks that the load is stable. She is:
o: describing and demonstrating safe use of hand and power tools and equipment

q: Why should a technician never rely on a jack alone to support a vehicle?
o: Jacks can fail or slip, so stands are needed

q: A shop collects used engine oil and coolant in labeled containers for a licensed recycler. This is:
o: proper handling and disposal of environmentally hazardous materials

q: Used coolant should not be poured on the ground because it:
o: is toxic and contaminates soil and water

o: where to begin testing, not always which part has failed

q: A technician explains that hydraulic fluid carries force through lines to move a lift and relieves pressure before work. She is describing:
o: hydraulic and pneumatic properties, controls and safety

q: Before disconnecting a hydraulic line, the technician should first:
o: loosen the fitting at full pressure

q: A parts clerk logs a fuel-injector order, shelves it by number and checks the bin counts weekly. She is describing:
o: parts management procedures such as ordering, stocking and locating

q: Keeping stock counts accurate helps a shop avoid:
o: running out of common parts and delaying repairs

q: An apprentice removes a cylinder head, inspects the gasket surface for warping and replaces the head gasket. She is demonstrating:
o: procedures for removal, inspection and replacement of engine components

o: inspection and maintenance of ancillary systems such as air intake and exhaust

q: A cracked boost hose can cause:
o: power loss and black smoke from leaking boost

q: Using a multimeter, a technician measures 12 V across a circuit with 4 amps flowing and calculates the resistance. She is applying:
o: electrical circuit testing, including Ohm's law

o: wiring diagrams and related symbols and service procedures

q: Wiring diagrams use symbols so that technicians can:
o: read a circuit without tracing every wire by hand

q: A technician checks the lift gate hydraulics and the power take-off on a utility truck for leaks. She is:
o: discussing procedures to inspect and maintain auxiliary systems

q: A power take-off is used to:
o: run auxiliary equipment such as pumps from the engine

q: A technician inspects the clutch, driveshaft and brake linings on a dump truck and adjusts as needed. She is:
o: inspecting and maintaining chassis and power train components

q: A worn U-joint in a driveshaft commonly causes:
o: vibration and a clunk during acceleration

q: A technician flushes a radiator, tests the coolant and replaces an oil filter on a diesel engine. She is performing:
o: inspection and maintenance of cooling and lubrication systems

q: Mixing the wrong coolant type in a diesel engine can cause:
o: corrosion and clogging in the cooling system

q: A shop supervisor does a quarterly walk-through to check eyewash stations, fire extinguishers and waste storage. She is demonstrating:
o: the process to perform regular audits and inspections to maintain compliance

q: Regular safety audits in a diesel shop help to:
o: find hazards before someone gets hurt or the shop is fined

q: A senior diesel tech briefs a new hire on a job in short, clear spoken steps and asks for the plan back. This shows:
o: effective oral communication with people from varied backgrounds

q: During a shift change, a technician reports an unfinished repair to the next person by:
o: explaining what was done and what remains

q: After diagnosing a no-start, a technician writes a clear report listing readings, parts and labor. This shows:
o: effective written communication with people from varied backgrounds

q: Detailed written notes on a repair help later when:
o: the same problem returns or a warranty claim is filed

q: A technician converts 1.5 inches to millimeters while checking a bore diameter on a heavy-duty engine. She is demonstrating:
o: mathematical skills and precision measurements using metric and customary systems

o: the function of the major components of diesel powered vehicles and equipment

o: moves hydraulic fluid to power cylinders and motors

o: the function of chassis components such as braking, steering and transmission

o: keep the brake shoe clearance in range

o: diagnosing, repairing and replacing auxiliary equipment such as power take-offs and hydraulics

q: If a hydraulic cylinder drifts down while holding a load, the likely cause is:
o: internal leakage past a worn seal

o: locating, reading and interpreting schematics, charts and diagrams

o: performing precision measurements and using published specifications to diagnose component wear

o: give the allowed limits so a technician knows when a part is worn out

q: Before using an impact wrench on a lug nut, a technician checks the socket and wears eye protection. She is:
o: demonstrating safe use of hand and power tools and equipment

q: A cracked impact socket should be:
o: taken out of service and replaced

q: A mobile mechanic bags oily rags and takes used filters to a recycler instead of the dumpster. She is:
o: demonstrating the proper handling and disposal of environmentally hazardous materials

q: Used oil filters are drained before disposal to:
o: keep leftover oil from reaching landfill

A technician connects a manufacturer's laptop software to the engine control module to run a cylinder cutout test. She is:
o: performing the proper use of diagnostic tools and equipment

q: A cylinder cutout test helps a technician find:
A technician explains why compressed air and hydraulic oil need pressure-rated hoses and how stored pressure can hurt a person. She is demonstrating:
o: knowledge of hydraulic and pneumatic properties, controls and safety

q: A pinhole leak in a high-pressure hydraulic hose can:
o: inject fluid through skin, so it should be found with cardboard, not a hand

q: A parts lead enters a new filter shipment, assigns a bin and orders replacements when stock hits a minimum. She is:
o: demonstrating parts inventory management such as ordering, stocking and locating

q: A reorder point is set so that a shop:
o: orders before the last part runs out

q: After a compression test shows one weak cylinder, a technician pulls the head, replaces a burned valve and reassembles per spec. She is demonstrating:
o: procedures for diagnosis, removal, repair and replacement of engine components

q: After reassembling a cylinder head, bolts are tightened in sequence with a torque wrench to:
o: clamp the gasket evenly and prevent leaks

q: A technician diagnoses an air-brake system that builds pressure slowly and finds a leaking air line. She is:
o: diagnosing, servicing and repairing diesel equipment systems such as braking and steering

q: Slow air pressure build-up on a truck can point to:
o: an air leak or a weak compressor

q: A technician tests the alternator and battery when a truck's lights dim and the starter drags. She is:
o: diagnosing and repairing electrical and electronic systems such as starting and charging

q: A battery that reads 11.8 volts at rest is:
o: partly discharged and should be charged and tested

q: A technician checks refrigerant pressures and the compressor clutch on a cab air-conditioning system. She is:
o: demonstrating an understanding of the diagnosis, service and repair of air-conditioning systems

q: Air-conditioning refrigerant must be recovered rather than vented because it:
o: harms the environment and is regulated

q: After a hard shift, a technician diagnoses a slipping clutch and inspects the transmission and differential on a tractor. She is:
o: diagnosing, servicing and repairing chassis and power train systems

q: A burning smell and a slipping clutch point to:
o: a worn or overheated clutch disc

q: A technician replaces a leaking water pump and tests the oil pump pressure on a diesel engine. She is:
o: servicing and repairing cooling and lubrication systems such as water pumps and oil pumps

q: Low oil pressure on a running diesel engine should be treated as:
o: an urgent warning to shut the engine down and find the cause

q: A technician connects a pressure gauge and a scan tool to a diesel fuel system to check rail pressure. She is:
o: using appropriate diagnostic equipment on various diesel equipment systems

q: Comparing measured fuel rail pressure to the specification lets a technician:
o: decide whether the fuel system is working correctly

q: A shop foreman logs fire extinguisher checks and updates the hazard communication binder every month. She is:
o: performing regular audits and inspections to maintain compliance with regulations

q: Keeping audit records helps a diesel shop:
o: show inspectors it follows safety and environmental rules
